albums.blurb: Portico Quartet came together busking on London's South Bank, building their sound around the hang — the bell-toned Swiss steel hand drum invented in 2000 — set against saxophone, double bass, and drums. Knee-Deep in the North Sea is the debut they recorded in 2007 after moving off the street and into the studio, released on Babel and later picked up by Peter Gabriel's Real World label; its patient, chiming minimalism laid the groundwork for the more electronic direction of their later albums like Isla and Memory Streams.
albums.reception: The album was nominated for the 2008 Mercury Prize and named Time Out magazine's Jazz, Folk and World album of the year for 2007.

albums.blurb: Big Time is Angel Olsen's fifth studio album, released on Jagjaguwar in June 2022 and co-produced with Jonathan Wilson. After the towering orchestral synth-pop of All Mirrors (2019) and its stripped-down twin Whole New Mess, Olsen turned toward warm, pedal-steel-laced country-soul; the songs were written in the wake of her coming out and losing both of her parents within weeks of each other, which gives the record its mix of new-love brightness and grief.
albums.reception: Big Time holds a Metacritic score of 88 based on 23 reviews, indicating universal acclaim.

albums.blurb: Marcos Valle came up in Rio's mid-60s bossa nova wave — he wrote the standard 'Samba de Verão' ('So Nice') — but by the early 70s he had folded funk, soul, and psychedelia into his songwriting. Previsão do Tempo, released on Odeon in 1973 with the jazz-funk trio Azymuth as his backing band, is the peak of that period, moving between breezy samba, synth-driven grooves, and slow-burning funk under its famous swimming-pool cover photo.
albums.reception: Original pressings have become ultra-premium collector's items, and the album has been reissued on vinyl by Light in the Attic.
